## e04777b1f6d7

**Classification: suspected coverage gap / domain question, not a reproduced
label error.** No target files were changed.

Generator SHA-256:
`983f3880d4a93d0d786301f88fd12b4325408ed09621894f0a3a40e316d01223`.
Rule hash: `672d7e42ddc1`.

The full 12-stage battery is green. However, strict canonical support accepts a
canonical 9×14 example containing three four-cell objects, while 300 ordinary
generated draws—100 each for easy, medium, and hard, seed `1000`, sample indices
0–99—contain only five-cell objects. All 300 sampled inputs are unique and have
no self-check or strict-profile failures. The generator source also constructs
fixed pentomino families, so size four appears structurally unreachable in its
ordinary distribution.

Evidence is retained in
`checks/audit/e04777b1f6d7/object-size-coverage.json`; a compact canonical-size-4
plus generated-size-5 Racket batch is in
`checks/audit/e04777b1f6d7/size4-and-generated-input.json` and
`checks/audit/e04777b1f6d7/racket.json`.

This is finite evidence and may reflect an intentional abstraction in which
object size is irrelevant. I therefore do not claim a rule defect. The maintainer
should decide whether canonical object cardinality is part of the desired
training domain; if yes, add a size-4 branch and feature-coverage regression.
